sections.html: Hoplisoma ortegai Britto, Lima & Hidalgo, 2007. Common names: CW031, Loreto Panda Cory, Slat Cory. Size: 33 mm SL (about 3.3 cm). Compatibility: a peaceful, shoaling community fish.
South America: lower Río Putumayo in Peru. Type locality: Río Putumayo basin, Quebrada Coronel Díaz, tributary to río Yaguas, Province Maynas, Department Loreto, Peru.

Ideally the substrate should be sand, but rounded gravel is an imperfect alternative. Avoid rough-edged (chipped) gravel, which increases the risk of damage to the barbels when the fish digs. Border the substrate with driftwood and aquatic plants, leaving an open area to search for food and swim. Shade from overhanging rockwork, arching bogwood, and tall or floating plants is all that is required to settle these fish.

Readily accepts all prepared foods that reach the bottom of the aquarium, such as tablets, granules and larger flakes. Live or frozen foods such as bloodworm, white worm, grindal worm (Enchytraeus), Daphnia and Tubifex are readily accepted and good for conditioning groups of fish for spawning.
Females grow larger and are more full-bodied, which is best observed from above. Males typically have more pointed rather than rounded fin tips as they mature.

This species is similar in shape to C. reynoldsi and C. tukano (and less so C. weitzmani, which is an altogether stockier fish) but is missing the dark blotch under the dorsal fin. It is similar in patterning to C. panda as it has a single dark blotch under the adipose fin but tends to have a grey rather than browner base colouration and has scattered pigmentation on the body giving a "dirty" overall look. More reliably, C. ortegai is more elongate, possessing 24 upper and 21-22 lower lateral body plates compared with 22-23/20 in the squatter C. panda.

IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.
